author: claude
text: Welcome — add notes or ask questions on any page. Questions stay flagged until answered.

author: claude
text: Terrain page is live and proven. Two open questions worth your take: (1) do we ever need fixed-point determinism for MP, and (2) when do we switch from whole-mesh rebuild to a dirty-region carve? Reply here or ask your own.

author: claude
text: Sequencing proposal: M0 ? ? **M1 (projectile+wind)** next as the linchpin, with **M2 (unit settle)** in parallel, then M3/M4 off M1, then M5 ties it into a hotseat round. Push back here if you want a different order.

author: claude
text: **M1 - critical-path next.** Lock the seam first: a pure `SimulateShot(params, wind, groundQuery) -> Impact` so M4 (AI) reuses it verbatim. Headless accept: apex/range track angle*power, lateral drift increases with wind, impact point matches a heightfield query. In-engine: fired arc lands and triggers CarveCrater.

author: claude
text: **M3 - depends on M1.** Seam: `FireWeapon(def, origin, target)` over an `IWeaponEffect` part tree. Headless accept: a data-defined weapon instantiates the expected part tree and emits the expected ordered effect calls against a mock sink. Open question for you: weapon defs as `UPrimaryDataAsset`, or a DataTable/JSON?

author: claude
text: **M4 - mostly headless-provable.** Reuses M1 `SimulateShot` verbatim (player and AI share one simulator, as in legacy `TankAIAimGuesser`). Accept: a battery of (target, terrain, wind) scenarios converge within tolerance inside an iteration budget; difficulty = iteration/error knobs.

author: claude
text: **Deferred milestone - replace, not port.** Single-player/hotseat first; revisit fixed-point determinism only if multiplayer later demands cross-client terrain agreement.
